newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Coffee sees brisk 97 start, cocoa subdued.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Coffee sees brisk 97 start, cocoa subdued.

text.p: Coffee options garnered brisk plays this week amid volatile underlying futures but the cocoa options market was subdued, traders said.
"You've seen the volatilities moved up a few points as the market picked up...there's also very good volume and sizeable positions are being built-up," said one trader.
Coffee options volume has reached over 6,000 lots since the New Year as the futures market seesawed.
"When the market turns like this, this is the time when the trade especially uses options to take their positions for the next few months," the trader said.
"With the turn, people are selling puts, people are buying calls...," the trader added.
The main interest on Thursday focused on the March $1,200/$1,350 put spread.
"March is looking a bit steady on trade interest buying puts underneath the market," one floor trader said. "There's also a bit of buying on call spread on May."
May saw some call spread at $1,300/$1,400, he added.
Coffee futures rebounded sharply from life-of-contract low of $1,203 a tonne basis March on Tuesday to $1,303 on Wenesday on fund stop-loss buying, buoyed by bullish Brazilian crop news.
The market rose further on Thursday, trading at $1,325 in late dealings on persistent fund short covering.
Coffee options volatilities improved slightly as the futures market took an upward turn.
"Big moves in futures pushed up options vols slightly," another floor trader said.
"Over the Christmas period, the vols were 28 percent and went down to a low of 25 but went up to 26 on Wednesday.
"People were looking to buy out-of-the money calls before yesterday's upward moves," he said.
Interest on the cocoa options pit was lacklustre, with players paying more attention to the futures market.

"I think there's a general interest in the market for people to sell out-of-money puts on July and September but the problem is there is no forward market in cocoa because people are unwilling to make a forward market," he said.

Broker Sucden said in a daily commentary that with continued origin selling and now a sizeable spec short position in London, it was becoming tempting to buy the futures and buy a put as downwside protection.

"Our feeling is that basis May, the market has potential to test down to 850 stg but we would be keen scale-down buyers into that level," Sucden's report said. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
